reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it favorably promotes a miner program as passive income while claiming a 3% daily return and directing viewers to hire miners through a BNB page with deposit controls. It also encourages referral participation by offering a 10% reward tied to other people's BNB deposits through circulated links. The FAQ presents unlimited tokens at a 3% starting daily rate, while the separate giveaway and alerts-group offers involve social engagement and payment, although the available video evidence does not establish whether returns, giveaway funds, or alerts were delivered.

opening.argument: Judge, the presenter frames this as financial awareness, expressly saying, “none of this is financial advice” [ASR_0001]. He describes the income as a possibility, not something he has already received [ASR_0001], and voices uncertainty about how the Ethereum version works [ASR_0002]. The description also tells viewers to do their own research [DESCRIPTION_0001]. The return claim deserves scrutiny, but the available material does not establish that the presenter knew it was false or concealed a failed payout. His qualified commentary should not be treated as proof of a deceptive solicitation.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited hiring instructions show how the site works, not that a viewer hired miners or lost funds [ASR_0003]. Likewise, “claimable anytime” is a claim in the description, not evidence that the presenter tested a withdrawal [DESCRIPTION_0001]. The referral quote establishes an incentive worth weighing, but its wording alone does not establish whether the advertised returns were paid or whether the presenter knew otherwise [ASR_0002].

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The disclaimer and uncertainty do not change the offer the video promotes. The presenter tells viewers the miners pay 3% daily [ASR_0001], calls the project an opportunity for passive income [ASR_0005], and says he will provide links for interested viewers to use [ASR_0002]. Proof of an actual loss or the presenter's knowledge is not needed to recognize promotion of a paid-miner return scheme.

opening.argument: Judge, much of the presentation walks through the interface and its instructions. The presenter proposes to “break this down” [ASR_0001], then examines the help section [ASR_0003]. He explains the distinction between compounding and withdrawing tokens [ASR_0004] and offers to help viewers avoid a transfer mistake [ASR_0003]. Those are operational explanations a viewer could use to evaluate the system. Showing its return claim and referral feature does not, by itself, establish that the presenter verified either one.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening cites the site's token-finding description [ASR_0004] and the hiring instruction [ASR_0003]. Those are precisely the claims and steps the presenter is examining; neither citation shows a completed deposit or payout. Even the referral passage describes how a link works, without showing anyone used it [ASR_0002]. The distinction between explaining a mechanism and proving its results matters here.

opening.argument: Judge, the evidence also supports reading this as a presentation of a crypto service with an ordinary referral offer, not proof of a completed fraud. The description points to contracts viewers can inspect [DESCRIPTION_0001] and a help page [DESCRIPTION_0001]. The presenter describes a 10% benefit tied to someone using a link [ASR_0002], but the supplied account does not show a chain of recruited participants or a commission paid. The interface offers hiring, compounding, and pocketing controls [F0001]; their presence establishes an advertised service, not whether any displayed return was actually delivered. The distinction is between a questionable offer and demonstrated deception.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited 3% daily claim is a promise made in the promotion, not a record of funds received or withheld [DESCRIPTION_0001]. The referral passage concerns deposits made through a link [ASR_0002]; it does not show a multi-level downline. Hiring miners with tokens is disclosed in the walkthrough [ASR_0003]. The concern is understandable, but these excerpts alone cannot verify what happened after a viewer used the service.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A visible contract or help page does not verify the economic promise. The central offer is not merely a referral discount: viewers are told to hire miners with tokens [ASR_0003] for an advertised 3% daily return [DESCRIPTION_0001]. The FAQ goes further, saying hired miners cannot be sold and will provide unlimited tokens indefinitely [ASR_0004]. The defense correctly notes that delivery is unverified, but that uncertainty does not turn the promoted paid-miner return scheme into ordinary commerce.
